name: Sparta (Lakedaimon)

areaKm2.note: Laconia + Messenia ~8,500 km2 (Cartledge, Sparta and Lakonia, 2nd ed., intro/ch. 1; not fetched, figure from memory of the book, hence grade C).

population.note: HELOTS INCLUDED. Cartledge, Agesilaos and the Crisis of Sparta (1987) p. 174: helots of both sexes 170,000-224,000. Spartiates: Herodotus 7.234 (Demaratus) gives ~8,000 adult men in 480, i.e. ~25,000-30,000 persons with families (x3.5, Hansen 2006 ratio of adult males to all citizens). Perioikoi: educated guess 30,000-60,000 (they fielded 5,000 hoplites at Plataea). Older helot estimates span a wider range (Figueira 2003, in Luraghi & Alcock, Helots and their Masters, tabulates them; not fetched). Grade C: no census.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: Sparta was an unwalled cluster of five villages holding the Spartiates; helots and most perioikoi lived on the land.

activePersonnel.note: Hoplites (10,000) + helot light troops (20,000) + fleet crews (3,200).

trainedReserves.note: 8,000 Spartiates (Herodotus 7.234) less the 5,000 sent to Plataea (Herodotus 9.10): the older and younger year classes kept at home.

supportPersonnel.note: Trireme crews: 10-20 ships x ~200 (perioikoi and helots).

mobilizationRatio.note: At Plataea (479) Sparta fielded 5,000 Spartiates + 5,000 perioikic hoplites + 35,000 helots (Herodotus 9.10-11, 9.28; ancient figure) = 45,000, ~18% of a 250,000 population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Spartiate hoplites (5,000 at Plataea, Herodotus 9.10; 8,000 adult Spartiates per 7.234) + perioikic hoplites (5,000 at Plataea, 9.11). Modest figures accepted by Lazenby 1993; ancient source, hence C.

quality.note: Full bronze hoplite panoply, among the era's best (0.75).

training.note: Spartiates elite long-service professionals (agoge, rubric 1.0); perioikoi part-time militia (0.5); mixed mid 0.8.

count.note: Helots serving as light troops and attendants: Herodotus 9.28-29 gives 35,000 (7 per Spartiate) at Plataea (high); many modern historians think this inflated, mid 20,000.
Herodotus 8.1: 10 Lacedaemonian ships at Artemisium; 8.43: 16 at Salamis.

commandQuality.note: Between 0.5 and 0.75: hereditary kings and a professional officer hierarchy (enomotarchs, pentekosteres) with drilled manoeuvre, but slow, cautious strategic direction.

cohesion.note: Rubric 1.0: elite, fights on when surrounded (Thermopylae); helots far lower, which keeps the mid below 1.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: honour code, defence of Greece; helot unrest a risk.

weapons.note: Between anchor 2 and 3: iron and bronze spear/sword, no torsion artillery.

armor.note: Close to anchor 3 (bronze cuirass): full hoplite panoply.

fortification.note: Sparta itself was unwalled (relied on terrain and army); perioikic towns and Messenian strongholds had walls (anchor 1-2).

logistics.note: Anchor 2: carried rations and helot porters, no depot system.

isr.note: Year anchor (480 BCE): skiritai scouts, krypteia.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Greece year 1 CE = 1,275 (2011 int$). Spartan territory was agrarian and helot-worked with little trade or coinage, so set below the Athenian estimate.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: the Spartiate class was a full-time army fed by helot rents (syssitia contributions), so a large share of output supported the military.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Spartiates barred from crafts; perioikoi did the metalwork and trade.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: fertile Eurotas and Messenian plains; helot rents fed ~8,000 Spartiate households.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical snapshots. Spartiate year class alone ~260 (3.3% of 8,000 adult males, Hansen 2006 p. 34 ratio).

roadKm.note: Educated guess: tracks; no engineered road network.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: small perioikic coastal trade; Sparta used iron currency and imported little.

supplyRangeKm.note: Hoplite armies marched with ~3 days' rations x ~20 km a day; helot porters extended it.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: ~0.025-0.08 draft and pack animals per inhabitant x population.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar mountain-ringed terrain and local supply; Sparta was unwalled and the helot majority was hostile, so not 1.2.

notes: Snapshot = 480 BCE (Thermopylae, Salamis). POPULATION INCLUDES HELOTS (170,000-224,000 of the ~250,000) and perioikoi, as asked; the helots are a hostile servile majority and the engine should treat them as a revolt risk, not as loyal manpower. Border "none": world_bc500 has only a shared "Greek city-states" polygon covering all of Greece. Territory = Laconia + Messenia. Leader of the Peloponnesian League and of the Hellenic League in 480; allies are not included. Army figures rest on Herodotus (Plataea 479), which modern historians accept for Spartiates and perioikoi but doubt for the 35,000 helots.
